The concept of impulsive force unifies mental phenomena through a shared dynamical property: the capacity to instigate motion—whether physical or conceptual. This is formalized as \( F_{\text{impulse}} = m \cdot a_{\text{mental}} \), where \( m \) represents the cognitive mass and \( a_{\text{mental}} \) the acceleration of mental state change. The impulsive nature of consciousness implies that all mental states inherently carry a directive force, making it a core variable in both GSI’s Bayesian inference over actions and GSE’s state-space navigation. The directionality of this force varies across modalities, suggesting a vectorial structure \( \vec{F}_{\text{impulse}} \), which enables modeling of attentional drift and decisional bias. Pleasure and pain act as scalar modulators of this force, \( F_{\text{pleasure-pain}} \), providing a hedonic anchor for behavioral prediction. These primitives form a closed-loop system where sensory input generates impulsive states, which then evolve into actions through a combination of probabilistic inference and deterministic state transitions.
